findings.reason: Index construction happens at the old phase query gate, not at artifact ingestion. It touches only rows whose component equals the requested original component. The original list comprehension also visited every such row before returning, so missing ACK/request_id errors are not moved ahead of prior native/physics gates or other required components. required_components order is unchanged; STOP asks only motion.

A non-builtin-str query takes the exact old equality scan. If any matching-component ID is non-builtin-str, that entire component uses the old scan, preserving list/dict unhashable IDs and bool/int equality. A malformed matching-component ACK is touched in the same input order as the original first scan; malformed ACK in another unrequested component is never inspected. All indexed duplicate rows and insertion order survive; returned row objects are the originals.

phase_indices is local to one _audit_records invocation and its consumed parsed list is unchanged during the physical-quantum loop. It is not shared across fresh calls or based on object identity; no ACK entries or cached group lists are mutated by the unchanged consumer loop.

The map is created only after the complete declaration validation, including target_check integer(decision_sequence,1). These are builtin integer keys. Pub target selection still comes from the same validated declarations. Python dict comprehension preserves original iteration order and last assignment, exactly selecting old related[-1] even for repeated target sequences and later declarations; no new event-time filtering is introduced.

json object_pairs_hook receives a completed list of builtin string-key pairs. dict(items) preserves unique values/order, and len difference exactly detects repeated keys with the unchanged generic duplicate JSON member error. Nested values/parse_constant are decoded before either hook, so duplicate-vs-nested errors remain at the same decoding stage. Full canonical(value), raw/decoded SHA, tail checks, gzip path and source/stat handling remain untouched; overflow/depth/nonfinite validation is not removed or shortened.

Ten test method definitions cover full public canonical JSON/exception comparisons, missing/duplicate/reversed ACK, malformed unused/used component, prior physics error, nonstring IDs, last-declaration expression, fresh calls, strict JSON overflow/nonfinite/depth/duplicate ordering and unchanged AST. This reviewer did not execute or import any candidate or fixture, and makes no CPU PASS/timing/qualification claim.

equivalence_scope: Immutable replay inputs produced by the unchanged strict JSON parser (builtin values), including invalid JSON-domain forms. Arbitrary stateful custom Python objects, allocation failure/MemoryError timing, or concurrent mutation are not claimed as a new supported ingress.
